acceptanceCriteria: When a customer purchases a return trip ticket with a promo code applied, the Mozio confirmation email displays the promo code discount amount for both the outbound trip and the return trip.
The promo code discount amount shown for the return trip in the Mozio confirmation email matches the discount amount applied to the return trip line item in the order payload.

When the order contains multiple line items representing outbound and return trips, the Mozio email confirmation template iterates over all line items and renders the promo code discount amount for each trip segment independently.

When a promo code is applied to a return trip ticket and the discount amount for the return trip is zero or not applicable, the Mozio confirmation email either omits the promo discount line for the return trip or explicitly displays a zero-amount discount, consistent with how the outbound trip is handled.

When a customer purchases a one-way trip ticket with a promo code, the Mozio confirmation email continues to display the promo code discount amount correctly for the single trip, confirming no regression from the fix.

The promo code discount amount displayed for the return trip in the Mozio confirmation email is formatted consistently with the outbound trip discount display, including currency symbol, decimal precision, and label.

When the order payload contains a return trip with a fromStation and toStation that are reversed relative to the outbound trip, the Mozio email confirmation correctly associates the promo code discount amount with the corresponding return trip segment.

acceptanceCriteria: When a customer purchases a return trip ticket with a promo code applied, the Mozio dispatch report for the return trip segment includes the promo code discount amount in the `report.price.discount.amount` field, matching how the outbound trip dispatch is constructed.
The promo code discount amount in the return trip dispatch's `report.price.discount` matches the discount applied to the return trip line item in the order payload (same value and currency).

When the order contains multiple line items representing outbound and return trips, the dispatch construction iterates over all line items and populates `report.price.discount` independently for each trip segment's dispatch.

When a promo code is applied to a return trip ticket and the discount amount for the return trip is zero or not applicable, the dispatch report either omits `report.price.discount` or sets it to a zero-amount discount, consistent with how the outbound trip dispatch is handled.
When a customer purchases a one-way trip ticket with a promo code, the Mozio dispatch report continues to include the promo code discount amount correctly, confirming no regression from the fix.

The discount amount in the return trip dispatch report is formatted with the same currency and decimal precision as the outbound trip discount, ensuring `mapToSanitizedMozioDispatch` renders both consistently in the email template.

When the return trip has fromStation and toStation reversed relative to the outbound trip, the promo code discount amount is correctly associated with the return trip dispatch segment (not lost or misattributed to the outbound segment).
after.description: [Mozio] - The Promo code amount is NOT displayed as expected for Return trip tickets in the Mozio email confirmation. The root cause is in the dispatch construction mapper: when building Mozio dispatches for return trip line items, the promo code discount amount is not correctly populated into the dispatch's `report.price.discount` field. The downstream `mapToSanitizedMozioDispatch` function faithfully passes through whatever discount data exists in the source dispatch, so the email will display the discount correctly once the dispatch construction includes it for return trips.

notes: The bug is that promo code discount amount is missing or incorrect for return trip tickets in the Mozio email confirmation. The email data flows through mapToSanitizedMozioDispatch which reads discount from dispatch.report.price.discount. The root cause is likely in the mapper that constructs Mozio dispatches from order line items — create-reservations.mappers.ts already handles return-trip station swapping but may not correctly propagate the discount amount for return trip line items into the dispatch report. The sanitized dispatch mapper is a downstream consumer that will correctly reflect whatever discount data is present in the source dispatch, so the fix must ensure the discount is populated at dispatch construction time for return trips.

notes: Modified AC3 to remove the implementation phrase 'iterates over all line items' and replaced with an observable outcome: each dispatch independently contains its own discount data. Modified AC6 to remove the internal function name 'mapToSanitizedMozioDispatch' and reworded as an observable email rendering outcome. Added AC8 (end-to-end email rendering) because the original criteria only verify dispatch data but the story is about what the customer sees in the email. Added AC9 (discount object completeness) because the story focuses on 'amount' but the discount object likely has sibling fields that could also be missing for return trips. Added AC10 (order-level discount attribution) as an edge case where the discount source is the order rather than a line item, which could cause the return trip dispatch to incorrectly show the full order discount or nothing. Flagged AC4 for ambiguity around omit vs zero-amount behavior.
